narrative:
The 2020 Baltimore Orioles were a team that defied expectations in the strangest season baseball has ever seen. Playing in a pandemic-shortened 60-game sprint, the Orioles entered July with modest hopes and quickly showed flashes of something surprising — a gritty, competitive club capable of stealing games from division rivals. The early weeks were marked by genuine excitement, with catcher Pedro Severino launching a go-ahead bomb against the Yankees and Pat Valaika delivering clutch hits that suggested this team had a pulse.

August became the defining month of the Orioles' season, and it told two stories simultaneously. Anthony Santander emerged as the team's offensive heartbeat, clubbing home runs and driving in runs at a pace that gave Baltimore fans reason to believe. The team went 13-16 in August — not a winning record, but competitive enough to stay relevant. However, the bullpen, particularly Cole Sulser, became a recurring source of heartbreak. Sulser's name appeared time and again on the wrong side of the ledger, surrendering crushing home runs to the likes of Aaron Judge and Randal Grichuk at the worst possible moments.

September brought the Orioles back to earth. A 10-16 finish to the season extinguished any lingering playoff hopes, and the bullpen continued to falter down the stretch. Tanner Scott joined Sulser as a source of late-game misery, surrendering leads against the Blue Jays that should have been preserved. The Yankees — a constant thorn — delivered more damage in September as Gleyber Torres added to the Orioles' late-season woes.

Ultimately, the 2020 Orioles finished 25-35, a record that masks the genuine competitiveness they showed at times. Santander's breakout, Severino's contributions behind the plate, and moments of clutch hitting from players like Jose Iglesias hinted at a foundation being built. But a bullpen that consistently squandered opportunities and a run differential that barely dipped into the red told the story of a team that was not yet ready — one that showed enough to be interesting but not enough to contend.

chapters.title: Surprising Start
chapters.description: The Orioles open the sprint season with a competitive 3-3 July, highlighted by Pedro Severino's dramatic home run against the Yankees.

chapters.title: Santander Steps Up
chapters.description: Anthony Santander announces himself as Baltimore's offensive anchor with a trio of big hits, keeping the Orioles competitive through mid-August.

chapters.title: Bullpen Cracks
chapters.description: Cole Sulser's repeated late-game implosions — including a brutal three-run surrender against Toronto — begin to undermine the team's hard-fought gains.

chapters.title: Fighting to Stay Alive
chapters.description: The Orioles claw back momentarily with Jose Iglesias delivering a clutch single and Tanner Scott recording a key double play, but the wins are harder to come by.

chapters.title: September Fade
chapters.description: A 10-16 September buries any playoff hopes as the bullpen falters again and the Yankees inflict one final blow to close out a disappointing stretch run.
